text:
maria: quick heads-up, onboarding a community model (hf: community/whisper-ish-demo) — generation_config.json has weird keys and our RW defaults seem to get skipped when chat template has a prefix token.

aj: what do you mean by prefix token? an actual special token in the prompt?

maria: yea we added <SYS_START> ... <SYS_END> tokens in the chat template. In HF generation_config.json they set `repetition_penalty": 1.1` as a string (ugh), and top_k: null. On import we coerce strings -> numbers but if the template includes a special token placeholder the runtime appears to ignore repetition_penalty entirely for the first N tokens.

kevin: that matches a bug I saw from quantized bringups — if the prefix consumes the kv-cache branch (prefix stored separately) the sampling path uses fallback defaults. Repro?

maria: repro steps pasted below:
```bash
# hf->rw import
python tools/hf_import.py --model community/whisper-ish-demo --out models/community-whisper
# then start small local serve with quantized weights
./serve_local --model models/community-whisper --quantize int8
# send a chat with the template that has <SYS_START>
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"input": "<SYS_START>System: you are helpful<USER> Hello" , "max_new_tokens": 64}'
```
kevin: any logs?

maria: tail of runtime log:
```
W [sampler] fallback to default sampling params: temperature=0.8 top_p=0.95 rep_penalty=1.0 (incoming gen_cfg had rep_penalty=1.1)
I [tokenizer] replaced special token <SYS_START> -> <s> (id 50256)
E [inference] kv-cache: prefix stored in dedicated buffer, using prefix branch
```

aj: so two things: tokenizer maps special tokens to surrogate ids and we put that prefix into a separate cache. Our parameter merging runs earlier but when prefix branch is taken the sampler fetches params from the wrong context object.

sam: @maria can you share the original generation_config.json from HF? I want to see types.

maria: paste:
```
{
  "temperature": "0.7",
  "top_p": 0.92,
  "top_k": null,
  "repetition_penalty": "1.1",
  "do_sample": "true"
}
```

kevin: aha do_sample is a string too. Our import coerces those but the runtime has two dicts: `base_params` and `prefix_params`. The prefix_params were created before coercion in the import pipeline in some older codepath. If prefix_params retains uncoerced strings, the sampler `get_rep_penalty()` returns falsy and falls back to default.

aj: fix idea: ensure coercion happens at the last possible moment (right before sampler read) or unify param objects during import. Also add a unit test that constructs a chat template with special tokens and a generation_config.json with mixed types.

sam: agree. Also worth normalizing `top_k: null` -> `top_k: 0` (or absent) because some samplers treat null as truthy in JS bridge. Add a conversion doc in tools/hf_import.py.

maria: quick patch tested by me: https://git.internal/rw/patches/1234 — it forces numeric coercion on both param maps. Locally the earlier log becomes: `... rep_penalty=1.1` and outputs match HF baseline sampling behaviour.

kevin: nice. Can you open a PR with tests? also run quantized smoke (int8) and non-quantized to be safe.

maria: will do. FYI there's a second gotcha: HF chat templates sometimes put special tokens inside the user message (not top-level prefix). In that case we ensure they remain in prompt and don't trigger prefix branch. We should add a detector that flags when a reserved special token is used outside the expected prefix zone. Might save future confusion.

aj: +1 for detector and an import-time warning. Please include example warning text.

sam: I'll follow up and add a small tweak to metrics so env logs show whether sampler used base or prefix params for each request (hidden bool).

maria: thanks all — filing the PR now, will tag @kevin @aj for review. :pray:
